policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: ASV 'in parables unto them' renders both the base order and RP's αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς; English constituent order is fixed by its own syntax and does not report the Greek.

ASV 'I have made ready' is compatible with either the perfect ἡτοίμακα or the aorist ἡτοίμασα; the English present perfect regularly renders a Greek aorist, so the tense of the Vorlage is not recoverable.
ὃς μέν and ὁ μέν are equivalent correlatives; ASV 'one ... another' renders either and no note bears on the choice.
The second member of the same correlative pair: ASV 'another to his merchandise' is identical under ὃς δέ and ὁ δέ.
ASV 'to his own farm' renders ἐπί and εἰς alike with the same preposition; nothing in the English or the notes distinguishes them.

ASV 'But the king was wroth' has neither the participle 'when he heard' nor the demonstrative 'that king' that RP's Καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐκεῖνος requires, and supplies nothing in italics; the shorter base reading is what is rendered.
ἐάν and ἄν are orthographic variants of the same particle in this construction; ASV 'as many as ye shall find' is identical under either.

ASV renders 'all as many as they found', the quantitative correlative ὅσους, not the plain relative οὓς ('all whom they found'); the same chapter's 22:9 renders ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε with the identical 'as many as ye shall find'.
ASV 'the wedding was filled with guests' renders γάμος, the wedding feast; WH's νυμφών is the bridal chamber or hall and would not be called 'the wedding'.

Word order only: 'Then the king said' fixes subject before verb in English regardless of whether the Greek read ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν or εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεύς. The verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns 'servants/ministers'.
ASV has the single imperative 'cast him out into the outer darkness'; RP's ἄρατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἐκβάλετε would require a prior 'take him away', which the ASV neither prints nor supplies in italics.
λέγοντες and λέγοντας differ only in the case of the participle, i.e. in whether it agrees with the senders or the sent; ASV's bare 'saying' leaves the agreement unmarked.
ASV 'They say unto him, Caesar's' renders the dative αὐτῷ explicitly and without italics; WH's omission would leave 'They say' with no indirect object.

The verse's textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities read saying', puts anarthrous λέγοντες in the margin, so the ASV text 'Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection' renders the articular οἱ λέγοντες.
γήμας and γαμήσας are alternative aorist participles of the same verb with the same sense; ASV 'the first married' renders either.

ASV 'And after them all, the woman died' renders the connective already present in the base clause; the extra καί of Treg/RP is ascensive and need not surface in English, so its presence or absence is not recoverable.
Word order only: 'In the resurrection therefore' places the postpositive οὖν where English requires it, under either Greek order.
γαμίζονται and ἐκγαμίζονται are the simple and compound forms of one verb with the same sense; ASV 'nor are given in marriage' renders either.
The verse's textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities add of God', places the words in the margin; the ASV text reads only 'as angels in heaven' and so renders the omission.
ASV 'in heaven' uses no article either way; the presence of τῷ before οὐρανῷ leaves no trace in the English.

ASV prints two unitalicized occurrences, 'God is not the God of the dead': a nominative subject and a predicate noun, which is RP's ὁ θεὸς θεός. The base and WHmarg readings have a single θεός and would yield only 'He is not the God of the dead'.
ASV ends the verse 'asked him a question, trying him:' with no 'and saying'; RP's added καὶ λέγων is not rendered.
ASV 'And he said unto him' names no subject; RP's added Ἰησοῦς would give 'And Jesus said unto him', and the ASV supplies no italicized equivalent.
ASV 'with all thy soul' shows only the possessive; the Greek article in the prepositional phrase leaves no separate trace in English.
Same construction as the preceding article: 'with all thy mind' renders the phrase with or without τῇ.

ASV 'the great and first commandment' keeps μεγάλη before πρώτη; RP's πρώτη καὶ μεγάλη would give 'the first and great commandment'. Here the coordination is rendered word for word, so the order is visible in the English.
ASV opens 'And a second like unto it is this', rendering the connective δέ that WH omits; the verse's other note is classed alternative_rendering and bears only on English phrasing.

ASV 'a second like unto it is this' has both the dative complement of ὁμοία ('unto it', = αὐτῇ) and a separate demonstrative 'this'; WH's αὕτη supplies only the demonstrative and would leave ὁμοία without its complement.
ASV places the verb before the second subject, 'the whole law hangeth, and the prophets', matching κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται; RP's καὶ οἱ προφῆται κρέμανται would put both subjects before the verb.
Word order only: English 'call him Lord' is the required order for the verb and its double accusative whichever Greek arrangement stood behind it.
ASV 'The Lord said unto my Lord' needs the definite article in English regardless; the presence or absence of ὁ before κύριος is not recoverable from it.
ASV 'underneath thy feet' renders the preposition ὑποκάτω; RP's ὑποπόδιον is a noun and would give 'thy footstool'.
Word order only: 'to answer him a word' fixes the English order under either Greek arrangement of the infinitive and its pronoun.
